answer: Registration requires a quadratic burn paid from aged coins. The fee is N squared times the median epoch reward, where N is how many identities were created in the window, and payment must come from coins unmoved for many epochs. Those coins are ivory collateral, retired after one use, so they cannot back a second key. Auditors demand a payment-path echo and reject routes sharing a conduit with an existing account, treating the coin graph as a karst of hidden channels. A farm must age and burn a rapidly rising sum of distinct coins for every extra identity; a reused path slashes the cluster.
